bibl.title: A cortical circuit for gain control by behavioral state

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the circuit by which locomotion increases visual responses in mouse V1
span.quote: The neural circuits that transmit behavioral state to sensory cortex to produce this modulation are unknown.

span.label: what pathway carries behavioural state into sensory cortex to produce the gain change
span.quote: The neural circuits that transmit behavioral state to sensory cortex to produce this modulation are unknown.

span.label: identifies VIP interneurons as the necessary and sufficient element, driven by nicotinic input from basal forebrain, and proposes the circuit as a general mechanism for state-dependent cortical gain control
span.quote: These findings establish a cortical circuit for the enhancement of visual response by locomotion and provide a potential common circuit for the modulation of sensory processing by behavioral state.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: These findings establish a cortical circuit for the enhancement of visual response by locomotion and provide a potential common circuit for the modulation of sensory processing by behavioral state.

span.label: locomotion-driven gain modulation of visual cortex
span.quote: Notably, the visual response of mouse primary visual cortex (V1) is enhanced by locomotion, a tractable and accessible example of a time-locked change in cortical state.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: To determine the impact of activating VIP neurons on the visual response of V1 neurons, we performed extracellular recordings as described in Supplemental Information and alternated trials in which VIP neurons were optogenetically-activated (using a blue light, referred to as LED condition) with control trials (No LED condition)

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Locomotion drives VIP interneurons, which inhibit SST interneurons, thereby disinhibiting neighbouring excitatory cells and raising their visual gain
span.quote: The present study reveals that a specific type of GABAergic cortical neuron, the VIP neuron, transmits the signal of locomotion to the cortex and operates through disinhibition of another GABAergic cortical neuron, the SST cell, to enhance the responses of neighboring cortical excitatory neurons

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Acetylcholine released from basal forebrain depolarises VIP neurons directly via nicotinic receptors, carrying the behavioural-state signal into cortex
span.quote: These findings in vivo suggest that acetylcholine (ACh) activates VIP neurons directly through nAChR.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: PV neurons show mixed locomotion responses because their change is a second-order consequence of SST disinhibition rather than direct locomotor drive
span.quote: Because VIP neurons principally inhibit SST neurons, which then inhibit PV neurons, which also receive local excitation, the activity of PV neurons during locomotion would be expected to be heterogeneous, as a secondary effect of relieving the inhibition from SST neurons rather than a direct response to locomotary input.

span.label: VIP neurons inhibit SST neurons, releasing neighbouring excitatory cells - a disinhibitory circuit
span.quote: Our findings that VIP neurons are activated while SST neurons are inhibited during locomotion are in good agreement with the current consensus that VIP neurons mainly innervate SST neurons ( Lee et al., 2013 ), although different effects on SST neurons have also been reported

span.label: acetylcholine from the nucleus of the diagonal band depolarises VIP neurons directly through nicotinic receptors
span.quote: In the presence of tetrodotoxin (TTX), the depolarization induced by ACh was abolished by the nAChR blockers MEC & MLA (12.41±0.98mV vs. 2.61±0.26mV, p <0.01, Supplemental Figure 5B and C ), confirming the existence of direct nicotinic cholinergic responses in VIP neurons.

span.label: PV heterogeneity is explained as a secondary effect: VIP inhibits SST, SST inhibits PV, and PV also receives local excitation
span.quote: Because VIP neurons principally inhibit SST neurons, which then inhibit PV neurons, which also receive local excitation, the activity of PV neurons during locomotion would be expected to be heterogeneous, as a secondary effect of relieving the inhibition from SST neurons rather than a direct response to locomotary input.

span.label: the state signal is carried by a pathway distinct from the sensory one, which is why VIP responses persist in darkness
span.quote: A signal conveying behavioral state to sensory cortex would ideally not be confounded by the sensory response that it modulates.

span.label: the kinetics are slow and lack a fast component, so the receptor is likely non-alpha7 nicotinic
span.quote: No fast nAChR component like that shown in layer I inhibitory neurons ( Letzkus et al., 2011 ) was evident; our findings showed instead a response with slow kinetics resembling what has been found in ChAT positive bipolar neurons ( Arroyo et al., 2012 ). Therefore, it is likely that VIP neurons are activated by ACh through non-

span.label: photolytic damage of individual VIP cells by restricting the excitation beam to one cell diameter at a time, sparing nearby cells
span.quote: While the nearby non-VIP neurons still responded to visual stimulation, the enhancement of their activity by locomotion was significantly reduced (86±16% enhancement without photo damage versus 12±6% enhancement after photo damage;

span.label: Nicotinic blockade did not fully abolish the locomotion response, so other inputs must contribute.
span.quote: It should be noted, however, that the response of VIP neurons to locomotion in the absence of visual stimulation was not completely abolished by nAChRs antagonists, indicating that there are probably other sources of locomotory input to VIP neurons.

span.label: Rabies tracing is inefficient, so additional neuromodulatory inputs may have gone undetected.
span.quote: Although we found that VIP neurons receive input from NDB, they may also receive inputs from other neuromodulatory sources, which might not be revealed due to the low efficiency of the rabies virus mediated retrograde tracing.

span.label: In the barrel-cortex experiment whiskers were not immobilised, so sensory input was not fully removed.
span.quote: However, although the mice were running in darkness with no visual input, the whiskers were intact and the mice were free to move them.

span.label: The auditory-cortex recordings were made without adequate isolation of auditory input.
span.quote: Our setup was far from ideal in isolating auditory inputs, which might result in a lower level of cross-correlation

span.label: nicotinic blockade did not completely abolish the locomotion response, so other inputs exist
span.quote: It should be noted, however, that the response of VIP neurons to locomotion in the absence of visual stimulation was not completely abolished by nAChRs antagonists, indicating that there are probably other sources of locomotory input to VIP neurons.

span.label: rabies tracing is low-efficiency, so other neuromodulatory inputs may simply not have been revealed
span.quote: Although we found that VIP neurons receive input from NDB, they may also receive inputs from other neuromodulatory sources, which might not be revealed due to the low efficiency of the rabies virus mediated retrograde tracing.

span.label: in the barrel cortex experiment the whiskers were intact and free to move, so the result may not isolate locomotion
span.quote: However, although the mice were running in darkness with no visual input, the whiskers were intact and the mice were free to move them.

span.label: the auditory setup was far from ideal at isolating auditory input
span.quote: Our setup was far from ideal in isolating auditory inputs, which might result in a lower level of cross-correlation

span.label: the basal forebrain responds to many things besides locomotion, including females and water
span.quote: It should also be kept in mind that the basal forebrain responds to many different stimuli and may influence cortical response by modulating different populations of neurons. For example, the neurons in NDB and nearby nuclei have been found to respond to not only to locomotion but also to other stimuli such as females (in male mice) and water

span.label: other groups report different effects of locomotion on SST neurons
span.quote: Our findings that VIP neurons are activated while SST neurons are inhibited during locomotion are in good agreement with the current consensus that VIP neurons mainly innervate SST neurons ( Lee et al., 2013 ), although different effects on SST neurons have also been reported

span.label: the SST-hyperpolarisation-during-whisking result, used as evidence that the same circuit may run in another modality
span.quote: Considering the similar distribution pattern of VIP neurons through the cortical areas, and the broad projection of NDB to other cortical areas, we examined whether VIP neurons in other primary sensory cortices are also modulated by locomotion.

span.label: rabies virus monosynaptic retrograde tracing, imported to find the afferents of a genetically defined cell type
span.quote: Interestingly, such retrograde tracing identified the nucleus of the diagonal band of Broca (NDB), a basal forebrain nucleus enriched in cholinergic neurons, as a prominent source of input to upper layer VIP neurons in V1

span.label: gain control here means a multiplicative change in visual response with no change in orientation selectivity - the OSI is checked and unchanged in both the locomotion and the optogenetic case
span.quote: Running increases visual responses without changing stimulus selectivity (OSI) ( Niell and Stryker, 2010 ). In the present study, activating VIP neurons increased visual responses and also did not change OSI

span.label: behavioural state is operationalised as running speed on a floating ball, with stationary and running separated at 1 cm/s
span.quote: To our surprise, while non-VIP neurons ( Figure 1B , green arrow) showed only low-frequency spontaneous calcium spikes similar to those when the animal was stationary, the calcium responses of VIP neurons were greatly elevated during locomotion

span.label: central rather than peripheral is established by a negative control in LGN, not by an argument
span.quote: This increase was found to be central rather than peripheral because there was no similar increase in the lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN), which relays activity from the eyes to the cortex.

span.label: VIP, SST and PV are genetic labels here, not physiological inferences - the paper says electrophysiology alone cannot distinguish these cell types
span.quote: However, electrophysiology alone does not allow one to distinguish among the large variety of GABAergic neurons with distinct physiological functions

span.label: replicates → Niell and Stryker, 2010
span.quote: On average, running led to an increase of 37±7% in the calcium response ( Supplemental Figure 1G ), demonstrating that our in vivo calcium imaging system is able to reproduce the findings made electrophysiologically ( Niell and Stryker, 2010 ).

span.label: builds-on → Pfeffer et al., 2013
span.quote: A similar approach revealed that somatostatin (SST) neurons were inhibited by locomotion, consistent with a circuit in which VIP cells increase activity of neighboring excitatory cells by inhibiting their inhibitory input from SST cells ( Pfeffer et al., 2013 ).

span.label: extends → Lee et al., 2010
span.quote: Although it was previously shown that 5-HT3a receptor positive neurons, among which VIP neurons are a major population, are depolarized by nicotine and show no response to muscarine ( Lee et al., 2010 ), there was no direct evidence that ACh activates VIP neurons through nAChR.

span.label: synthesises-with → Pi et al. 2013 on VIP disinhibition in prefrontal and auditory cortex - a paper independently tagged in this corpus
span.quote: It has recently been shown that VIP neurons also inhibit SST neurons in prefrontal and auditory cortices, and that activating VIP neurons increases auditory responses ( Pi et al., 2013 ). Combining these with present findings suggests that VIP-neuron-mediated disinhibitory circuit is the, or at least a principal, mechanism of gain control by behavioral state in sensory cortices.

span.label: extends → Niell and Stryker's finding that locomotion increases V1 gain without changing selectivity
span.quote: On average, running led to an increase of 37±7% in the calcium response ( Supplemental Figure 1G ), demonstrating that our in vivo calcium imaging system is able to reproduce the findings made electrophysiologically

span.label: supports → Pfeffer et al. on VIP neurons inhibiting SST neurons
span.quote: Our findings that VIP neurons are activated while SST neurons are inhibited during locomotion are in good agreement with the current consensus that VIP neurons mainly innervate SST neurons ( Lee et al., 2013 ), although different effects on SST neurons have also been reported

span.label: contradicts → the expectation of substantial direct motor cortex input to V1 VIP neurons
span.quote: While we labeled more than 50 upper layer VIP neurons in V1, only 0–1 neurons per mouse were retrogradely labeled in motor cortex or the border between motor and cingulate cortex ( Figure 5G ), suggesting at most very sparse direct input from motor cortex.

span.label: distinguishes-from → the run-onset neurons of Keller et al., which respond only transiently
span.quote: A previous study also reported that some neurons are activated during running in darkness ( Keller et al., 2012 ). The neurons identified in that study are unlikely to be VIP neurons because they responded only briefly to some of the onsets and offsets of running, while we find that VIP neurons respond faithfully and tonically to all running episodes.

span.label: qualifies → its own cholinergic account, by noting noradrenergic input as a likely additional source
span.quote: The fact that we were not able completely to block the response of VIP neurons to locomotion using nicotinic antagonists makes a role for other neuromodulatory inputs seem likely. For example, a recent study suggested a role of noradrenergic input

span.label: VIP —causes→ SST
span.quote: Our findings that VIP neurons are activated while SST neurons are inhibited during locomotion are in good agreement with the current consensus that VIP neurons mainly innervate SST neurons ( Lee et al., 2013 ), although different effects on SST neurons have also been reported

span.label: locomotion —causes→ VIP
span.quote: In vivo calcium imaging of behaving animals revealed that locomotion activates vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP)-positive neurons in mouse V1 independent of visual stimulation and largely through nicotinic inputs from basal forebrain.

span.label: basal forebrain —causes→ VIP
span.quote: In vivo calcium imaging of behaving animals revealed that locomotion activates vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP)-positive neurons in mouse V1 independent of visual stimulation and largely through nicotinic inputs from basal forebrain.

span.label: VIP —causes→ gain control
span.quote: Taken together, these findings indicate that VIP neuron activation is both necessary and sufficient for the increase in the visual response of excitatory cells produced by locomotion.

span.label: gain control —operationalised-as→ orientation selectivity index
span.quote: Running increases visual responses without changing stimulus selectivity (OSI) ( Niell and Stryker, 2010 ). In the present study, activating VIP neurons increased visual responses and also did not change OSI

span.label: SST —causes→ PV
span.quote: Because VIP neurons principally inhibit SST neurons, which then inhibit PV neurons, which also receive local excitation, the activity of PV neurons during locomotion would be expected to be heterogeneous, as a secondary effect of relieving the inhibition from SST neurons rather than a direct response to locomotary input.

span.label: correlation
span.quote: Analysis of all VIP neurons imaged under conditions of no visual stimulation by calculating the cross-correlation between the calcium signal and running speed revealed a single positive peak around time zero (0.47±0.03, mean±SEM, n=28)

span.label: Mann-Whitney U test
span.quote: Interestingly, we found that the cross-correlation between the VIP neurons’ calcium responses and locomotion was not increased by visual stimulation with moving bars, and indeed was significantly reduced (0.28±0.03, mean±SEM, n=44, p <0.0001 comparing with no visual stimulation group, Mann-Whitney U-test)

span.label: paired t-test
span.quote: Furthermore, the average calcium signal of SST neurons was consistently reduced by running ( Supplemental Figure 3D , left panel, normalized signal during running vs. stationary, p <0.001, paired t-test)

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: On average, the zero-time cross-correlation of VIP neurons was 0.58±0.03 (n=21), significantly different from that of PV neurons (0.30±0.06, n=40, p =0.01, rank-sum test), and SST neurons was −0.19±0.05 (n=11, p <0.005 comparing with 0, t-test), which were also different from each other ( Figure 3D , p <0.0001, one-way ANOVA)

span.label: Wilcoxon rank-sum test

span.label: VIP neurons in mouse V1 are activated in tight correlation with locomotion even in complete darkness, unlike nearly all neighbouring non-VIP neurons.
span.quote: We found that the neural activity of VIP neurons in mouse V1 is closely correlated with the locomotion even without visual stimulation, when most other neurons in the visual cortex show only spontaneous activity.

span.label: Adding visual stimulation did not strengthen the VIP-locomotion coupling; it significantly weakened it, so the locomotion signal is not confounded with the sensory response it modulates.
span.quote: Interestingly, we found that the cross-correlation between the VIP neurons’ calcium responses and locomotion was not increased by visual stimulation with moving bars, and indeed was significantly reduced (0.28±0.03, mean±SEM, n=44, p <0.0001 comparing with no visual stimulation group, Mann-Whitney U-test)

span.label: The three inhibitory classes respond differently to running: SST neurons are suppressed, PV neurons respond heterogeneously, and VIP neurons are consistently driven.
span.quote: The average cross-correlation of SST neuron activity with locomotion was negative at time-zero, and the distribution of zero-time cross-correlation had a single negative peak

span.label: Blocking nicotinic cholinergic receptors locally in V1 removed most of the VIP locomotion response, while blocking glutamatergic input did not.
span.quote: The local blockade of nicotinic cholinergic input, but not of glutamatergic input, reduced the response of VIP neurons to locomotion by more than two thirds, and measurements in vitro disclosed powerful nicotinic cholinergic input to VIP neurons.

span.label: Monosynaptic rabies tracing identified the cholinergic nucleus of the diagonal band of Broca in basal forebrain as a direct input source to upper-layer V1 VIP neurons.
span.quote: Interestingly, such retrograde tracing identified the nucleus of the diagonal band of Broca (NDB), a basal forebrain nucleus enriched in cholinergic neurons, as a prominent source of input to upper layer VIP neurons in V1

span.label: Optogenetically driving VIP neurons in stationary mice reproduced the locomotion-induced gain increase, and selectively killing VIP neurons removed it.
span.quote: Optogenetic activation of VIP neurons increased V1 visual responses in stationary awake mice, artificially mimicking the effect of locomotion, and photolytic damage of VIP neurons abolished the enhancement of V1 responses by locomotion.

span.label: The gain-and-loss experiments together establish VIP activation as both necessary and sufficient for the locomotion-driven enhancement of excitatory visual responses.
span.quote: Taken together, these findings indicate that VIP neuron activation is both necessary and sufficient for the increase in the visual response of excitatory cells produced by locomotion.

span.label: VIP neurons in somatosensory and auditory cortex are also modulated by locomotion, though more weakly than in V1, suggesting a general cortical arrangement.
span.quote: The responses of VIP neurons in primary auditory cortex were also associated with locomotor activity

span.label: Locomotion raises response gain without altering orientation tuning, and optogenetic VIP activation reproduced this selectivity-preserving profile.
span.quote: Running increases visual responses without changing stimulus selectivity (OSI) ( Niell and Stryker, 2010 ).

span.label: VIP neurons track locomotion in complete darkness, when neighbouring neurons show only spontaneous activity
span.quote: To our surprise, while non-VIP neurons ( Figure 1B , green arrow) showed only low-frequency spontaneous calcium spikes similar to those when the animal was stationary, the calcium responses of VIP neurons were greatly elevated during locomotion

span.label: VIP neurons are the majority of locomotion-responsive cells in V1 in the absence of visual stimulation
span.quote: While 20/28 imaged VIP neurons had a zero-time cross-correlation larger than 0.4, only 3/77 non-VIP neurons had a zero-time cross-correlation larger than 0.4 ( Figure 2C ), indicating that VIP neurons constitute the majority of the neurons responsive to locomotion in the absence of visual stimulation in mouse V1.

span.label: visual stimulation does not increase, and in fact reduces, the coupling between VIP activity and locomotion
span.quote: Interestingly, we found that the cross-correlation between the VIP neurons’ calcium responses and locomotion was not increased by visual stimulation with moving bars, and indeed was significantly reduced (0.28±0.03, mean±SEM, n=44, p <0.0001 comparing with no visual stimulation group, Mann-Whitney U-test)

span.quote: On average, running led to an increase of 37±7% in the calcium response ( Supplemental Figure 1G ), demonstrating that our in vivo calcium imaging system is able to reproduce the findings made electrophysiologically

span.label: VIP 0.58 plus or minus 0.03, PV 0.30 plus or minus 0.06, SST -0.19 plus or minus 0.05 — zero-time cross-correlation with locomotion by cell type
span.quote: On average, the zero-time cross-correlation of VIP neurons was 0.58±0.03 (n=21), significantly different from that of PV neurons (0.30±0.06, n=40, p =0.01, rank-sum test), and SST neurons was −0.19±0.05 (n=11, p <0.005 comparing with 0, t-test), which were also different from each other ( Figure 3D , p <0.0001, one-way ANOVA)

span.label: 20/28 VIP versus 3/77 non-VIP neurons above 0.4 correlation — how specific the locomotion response is to VIP cells
span.quote: While 20/28 imaged VIP neurons had a zero-time cross-correlation larger than 0.4, only 3/77 non-VIP neurons had a zero-time cross-correlation larger than 0.4 ( Figure 2C ), indicating that VIP neurons constitute the majority of the neurons responsive to locomotion in the absence of visual stimulation in mouse V1.

span.label: 32.4 plus or minus 8.3% — increase in visual response from optogenetic VIP activation
span.quote: Photo-activation of VIP neurons in awake stationary mice significantly increased the visual response of layer 2/3 neurons by 32.4±8.3% (mean±s.e.m.; n=19, p <0.02, paired Wilcoxon signed rank test) without producing locomotion or changing the orientation selectivity index (OSI)

span.label: 86 plus or minus 16% before versus 12 plus or minus 6% after photo damage — locomotion enhancement lost when VIP cells are destroyed
span.quote: While the nearby non-VIP neurons still responded to visual stimulation, the enhancement of their activity by locomotion was significantly reduced (86±16% enhancement without photo damage versus 12±6% enhancement after photo damage;

span.label: 0 to 1 neurons per mouse in motor cortex against more than 50 labelled VIP neurons — the near-absence of direct motor input
span.quote: While we labeled more than 50 upper layer VIP neurons in V1, only 0–1 neurons per mouse were retrogradely labeled in motor cortex or the border between motor and cingulate cortex ( Figure 5G ), suggesting at most very sparse direct input from motor cortex.
